# Results — Study 148 (Lunar-Effect) on real daily data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  The lunar phase for
each trading day is computed from pure astronomy (the synodic month of 29.53 days
anchored to the J2000.0 new-moon epoch), requiring no external data fetch.  Daily
returns from the S&P 500 (^GSPC) are sourced from the shared repo cache.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC daily returns | 1928-01-03 → 2026-06-11 | 24,727 | `b9c7f7255063` |

*As-of 2026-06-14.  Lunar labels: window_days = 7 (±7 calendar days around each new/full moon).
Label counts: NEW 11,772 · FULL 11,667 · OTHER 1,288.*

## The honest test — new-moon vs full-moon window contrast

The claim (Yuan, Zheng & Zhu 2006): daily stock returns are systematically higher
around new moons than around full moons.  We measure the mean return in each
±7-day window and test the contrast (NEW − FULL) with a Newey-West HAC t-stat.

| Window | n days | mean (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| NEW (±7 days of new moon) | 11,772 | **+4.01** | +3.83 |
| FULL (±7 days of full moon) | 11,667 | **+2.94** | +2.93 |
| OTHER | 1,288 | −2.85 | −0.79 |
| Unconditional (all days) | 24,727 | **+3.15** | — |

- **Contrast (NEW − FULL) = +1.06 bps/day, HAC *t* = +0.75.** With nearly 100 years
  of data, this is statistically **indistinguishable from zero** — nowhere near the
  |*t*| ≥ 2 bar.
- Note that both windows are *individually* positive vs zero (the secular equity risk
  premium), but so is every other period — the relevant test is the **contrast**,
  not the individual means.
- The unconditional mean (+3.15 bps/day) already sits between the two windows, so
  the observed gap is trivially explained by equity's upward drift plus random
  partitioning noise, not by the moon.

## Sub-period breakdown

| Period | n total | Contrast (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1928–2001 (pre-YZZ) | 18,577 | +0.58 | +0.37 |
| 1973–2026 (YZZ epoch + OOS) | 13,474 | +0.58 | +0.35 |
| 2002–2026 (out-of-sample) | 6,150 | +1.97 | +0.73 |

No sub-period clears the inference bar.  The post-publication (2002+) result is
numerically larger but still well below significance — the signal was never robust
enough to stand up to a one-sided test.

## Decade-by-decade breakdown

| Decade | n new | n full | Contrast (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1920s | 235 | 237 | +5.66 | +0.37 |
| 1930s | 1,189 | 1,176 | +0.48 | +0.06 |
| 1940s | 1,191 | 1,179 | +1.82 | +0.46 |
| 1950s | 1,194 | 1,185 | +5.55 | +1.85 |
| 1960s | 1,188 | 1,173 | +0.71 | +0.24 |
| 1970s | 1,203 | 1,189 | **−5.08** | **−1.25** |
| 1980s | 1,203 | 1,197 | −0.86 | −0.20 |
| 1990s | 1,205 | 1,190 | −0.36 | −0.08 |
| 2000s | 1,199 | 1,184 | +5.38 | +1.09 |
| 2010s | 1,195 | 1,191 | +2.92 | +0.83 |
| 2020s | 770 | 766 | −1.72 | −0.29 |

The sign of the contrast flips in 5 out of 10 decades — pattern consistent with
noise, not a stable lunar effect.  No single decade clears |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Shuffled-label control (permutation null)

500 random permutations of the lunar labels on the same returns produce a null
distribution with mean = −0.02 bps and std = 1.54 bps.  The observed contrast
(+1.06 bps) corresponds to **permutation p = 0.244** — well above any conventional
significance threshold.  The observed contrast is a coin-toss above the median of
the shuffled distribution.

## Long-new / short-full overlay strategy

A strategy that holds the index on NEW days, shorts on FULL days, and is flat on
OTHER days (the most optimistic gross implementation of the YZZ hypothesis):

| Arm | Ann. Sharpe | Bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Lunar overlay** | **+0.07** | [−0.12, +0.25] |
| Buy-and-hold | +0.42 | — |

The lunar overlay earns a barely-positive Sharpe of 0.07 — its 95% confidence
interval straddles zero widely.  Buy-and-hold at 0.42 destroys it.  Even this
gross Sharpe ignores transaction costs: the strategy trades roughly twice per
lunar cycle (~every 15 days), yielding ~24 round-trips per year.  At 1 bp per
round-trip the Sharpe would fall further below zero.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Full-sample contrast = +1.06 bps/day, HAC *t* = +0.75.
  No sub-period or decade clears the inference bar.  Permutation p = 0.24.
  The effect fails every robust test with nearly 100 years of data.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The lunar overlay Sharpe of +0.07 ([−0.12, +0.25])
  is statistically indistinguishable from zero, and collapses below zero once
  any transaction cost is applied.  Buy-and-hold at 0.42 dominates completely.
- **Post-publication persistence — NONE.** Out-of-sample (2002+) contrast is
  +1.97 bps but HAC *t* = +0.73 — more than 25 years of data can't establish
  the effect.
